pages.title: Equilibrium and direction of motion
pages.text:
Equilibrium and direction of motion
M∗ = r/k, ˙M = k(M∗ − M ).
For r = 2, k = .25, the equilibrium is 8 mg. Below it the mass rises; above it the mass
falls.

pages.title: Convex-combination form
pages.text:
Convex-combination form
M (t) = e−ktM0 + (1 − e−kt)M∗.
Nonnegative weights summing to one imply positivity and conﬁnement between the two
endpoints.

τ = 1/k, θ = kt, m = M/M∗ (r > 0).

en = Mn − M∗, e n+1 = (1 − kh)en.
en = (1 − kh)ne0.
A negative multiplier alternates the side of equilibrium.

pages.title: Stability interval
pages.text:
Stability interval
|1 − kh| < 1 ⇐ ⇒0 < kh < 2.
The subinterval 1 < kh < 2 is stable but oscillatory.

Positivity of the Euler update
Mn+1 = (1 − kh)Mn + hr.

pages.title: Numerical and physical discrepancies
pages.text:
Numerical and physical discrepancies
Compare ﬁrst with the exact equation solution, then with independent observations.
A small numerical error does not establish the mixing or proportional-removal assumptions.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 19 / 19
